chapter: Band building and learning from musicians
title: Guest lecturers: New Orleans musicians sitting in
summary: DeVore explains how visiting players such as Jim Robinson or Kid Thomas could teach tone and phrasing by playing with a student band.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Say we've got Paul setting them up like that. What about having guest lecturers?

That's invaluable because for instance you have maybe Jim Robinson come by. He hears the band and you've set the band up and you've got this so far. You've got a blues going medium tempo and you've got everybody doing this. Very simple and it would be very stiff. Then you slip Jim in there and say Jim this is with the band. What would you do playing along with us? The tromboman would drop out and Jim would start playing and he was going all the things that Jim does. Then a tromboman could really begin to get some understanding of these things. Probably after you got this down regardless of what kind of tone you use or what kind of attack you use then you could work on the tonality and the attack and the phrasing. The only way that a guy can really understand that is by listening to the New Orleans men on record or having them right there. That's what you would need a man on the job for to be a New Orleans man to come in and help you. That's where you could utilize his he wouldn't have to explain anything. All he had to do was just play because if the man you had in your band was playing a simple melody like you tell me your dream and he knew the melody straight through then you'd have maybe another man the trumpet man like Kid Thomas come in and he played the way he plays it and then he could tell the way Tom's tonality the type of tone he gets and he could ask Tom how he did this and the way Tom phrased and he could also ask him about that and Tom most likely could be able to answer them. I was thinking the New Orleans men would be able to teach in this respect from demonstration in the same way with clarinet men. Well I think
that some of the New Orleans guys are pretty good talkers too.
